technology_decision: Retain explicit Python validation for CalibrationRecord admission: fixed field/tuple checks preserve raw JSON-compatible values and digest bytes; a guarded Pydantic/Rust-core candidate passed the same tests but showed no consistent material CPU benefit and requires normalization safeguards.
scope: P1.3 calibration admission only; clock mapping and acquisition/decoder/inference/process-isolation technology reviews remain open.
requirements: Nonnegative integer times and positive integer dimensions; matching nonempty calibration/mount identities.
Only a numeric nine-element identity tuple and finite residual in the unchanged inclusive [0, 0.05] interval.
Expiry remains inclusive; malformed data must return False before build_v3 emits registered observations; no digest-input coercion.

research.assessment: Dataclass fields alone do not validate runtime types; explicit admission checks can preserve the existing immutable representation and digest.

Compiled strict tuple schemas are a viable alternative. The executed candidate checks metadata natively and adds an exact numeric guard because strict float validation can accept non-JSON numeric objects.

CUE provides declarative bounds, closed schemas, a CLI and Go API. Investigated independently of installed tools. JSON transport cannot distinguish the existing tuple-only transform from a list (identical serialized bytes), so a process/Go bridge still needs representation checks or a new tagged boundary. Not selected for this in-memory admission gate; no CUE performance claim or general exclusion.

checks.red: 66 incorrect acceptances and 6 exceptions before implementation
checks.hosted: Six installed OS/Python jobs extended with calibration regression and guarded schema comparison; execution pending.

negative_candidate_result: Initial strict schema accepted Decimal residual while unchanged digest raised TypeError. Explicit number guard fixed candidate parity; regression retained.
limitations: Shared Mac diagnostic CPU results vary; no hard latency, physical calibration, RSS or deployment qualification claim.
Tracemalloc excludes native allocations; the candidate traced fewer Python bytes (304 vs 456), not proof of lower total memory.
One representational/validation boundary was compared, not entire worker architectures or every language.
Full release qualification and all previous negative gates remain pending.
